articles.title: The requester is not the reader: engineering for someone who will never file a bug
articles.excerpt: The request came out as one long sentence, and it was a good sentence: every morning at seven, three to five things that have to do with her — weather, food prices, buses, the doctor; no words she won…
articles.body: The request came out as one long sentence, and it was a good sentence: every morning at seven, three to five things that have to do with her — weather, food prices, buses, the doctor; no words she won't understand; one item, one short paragraph; short enough that she can read it out loud. Then, at the very end, almost as an afterthought: not too long. At twenty past seven the next morning the phone rang. She had read it, got halfway, gone out to buy vegetables, come back, and finished it. The verdict travelled back word for word: she went out to buy vegetables halfway through. Make it shorter. There is a version of that exchange that is a story about a mother, a son, and a tablet he bought her six months earlier which now has two uses left — the photos and scrolling.

articles.title: How to write good commit messages and PR descriptions fast on a Mac
articles.excerpt: Most of us know what a good commit message looks like. We just don't write one at 6 PM when the tests finally pass. The fix isn't more willpower. It's setting up your Mac and Git so the good version i…
articles.body: Most of us know what a good commit message looks like. We just don't write one at 6 PM when the tests finally pass. The fix isn't more willpower. It's setting up your Mac and Git so the good version is the easy one: a template that asks the right questions, an editor that opens instantly, your diff right in front of you while you write, and a pull request description that mostly fills itself in. Here's the setup I use, step by step. Everything below uses stock Git, the GitHub CLI, and tools that ship with macOS. 1. Stop using -m for anything that matters git commit -m "fix stuff" is fast because it skips the editor, and that's the problem: a one-liner is the only thing it encourages. Keep -m for truly trivial commits (a typo, a version bump) and let Git open an editor for everything else.

articles.title: Rotating vs. Sticky Proxy Sessions: Which One Should You Use for Web Scraping?
articles.excerpt: More IP rotation isn't always better for web scraping. If you're collecting data from hundreds of independent product pages, rotating IPs can make sense. But if your scraper needs to move through seve…
articles.body: More IP rotation isn't always better for web scraping. If you're collecting data from hundreds of independent product pages, rotating IPs can make sense. But if your scraper needs to move through several pages while keeping the same session, switching IPs too often can create problems. The tricky part is that neither option is universally better. It depends on how your scraper interacts with the target website. Here's how I'd approach the choice. Rotating Proxies: Better for Independent Requests Rotating proxies change the outgoing IP address according to the provider's rules. Depending on the setup, the IP might change with each request, after a set interval, or when a new session starts. They're a practical option when you're collecting data from many independent URLs.

articles.title: How I Turned AI Writing Tells into a Pre-Read Quality Gate
articles.excerpt: If a draft is going to sound machine-made, I want to catch it before an editor spends time on it. That is the idea behind a small “humanizer skill” I use in my content workflow: every AI draft starts…
articles.body: If a draft is going to sound machine-made, I want to catch it before an editor spends time on it. That is the idea behind a small “humanizer skill” I use in my content workflow: every AI draft starts at 100, then loses points for each writing tell the rubric detects. It is not a magical detector, and it is not trying to prove authorship. It is a practical gate that helps my team decide whether a draft is ready for a human reader, needs a rewrite, or should be rebuilt from scratch. The detail that makes the whole thing useful is also the easiest to overlook: the rubric is not built around vague “AI vibes.” It is based on specific patterns.
articles.author: Lena Brooks

articles.title: A Node.js Gate Before Private Object Storage File Delivery
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Keep export objects private, authenticate the person requesting the download, and redirect that request to a newly minted, short-lived presigned URL. A Node.js application should store an export…
articles.body: TL;DR Keep export objects private, authenticate the person requesting the download, and redirect that request to a newly minted, short-lived presigned URL. A Node.js application should store an export record rather than a durable object URL; that record is where tenant authorization, expiry, and audit decisions belong. The least complex design is an authenticated application endpoint followed by a redirect to object storage. It removes the application server from the data path without turning a forwarded link into a long-lived grant. The signature is useful, but it is only one boundary in a file-export system.

articles.body: On October 21, 2026, PHP shipped emergency releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. They fix two flaws in PHP itself, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that the PHP project says can allow unauthenticated remote code execution: someone with no login running their own code on your server. Both are rated Critical, 9.2 on CVSS v4.0. The short answer: find the PHP version that actually serves your website. If it is older than the fixed release in the table below, update it today. Information current as of October 21, 2026, 14:30 UTC. Vendor status is changing by the hour; check the linked sources. Which PHP versions are affected by PHP2Shell? Every PHP branch in use is affected. Wiz Research , which found and reported the bugs, says every PHP version back to 5.4 has at least one of them.

articles.title: NASA’s CASALS Instrument Bridges Gaps in 3D Maps of Earth’s Surface
articles.excerpt: From orbit, today’s space-based laser instruments measure Earth’s forests and terrain one narrow line at a time. Between those lines are enormous gaps that include millions of acres of land scientists…
articles.body: Explore This Section Overview Technology Programs Technology Highlights Workshops and Events Publications From orbit, today’s space-based laser instruments measure Earth’s forests and terrain one narrow line at a time. Between those lines are enormous gaps that include millions of acres of land scientists never directly measure. NASA’s CASALS instrument will blend machine learning with an ultra-compact lidar instrument to adaptively ‘sweep’ large swaths of Earth’s surface. This new capability for space-based remote sensors allows CASALS to create truly three-dimensional (3D) topographical renderings.
